The US government turned off Anthropic's most powerful AI models. A week later, they're still offline worldwide.

Fable 5 and Mythos 5 — two frontier models that thousands of businesses built workflows around — were shut down by federal order. No confirmed restoration date exists. At the G7 summit in France on June 17, the CEOs of Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and OpenAI sat with President Trump and world leaders, but the shutdown was the conversation nobody had publicly.

This is not a hypothetical risk scenario from a consultant's slide deck. This actually happened. A government decision made a major AI vendor's top capabilities disappear from production overnight.

The silver lining: the open-source ecosystem responded immediately. Moonshot AI released Kimi K2.7 Code — a trillion-parameter model with drop-in OpenAI API compatibility. Z.ai shipped GLM-5.2 under a fully permissive MIT license with a million-token context window. For teams that need to move fast, frontier-grade alternatives are live and testable today.

The lesson is clear. If your AI strategy depends on a single vendor, you are carrying risk that is no longer theoretical. Multi-model architectures and open-weight fallback layers need to be part of every serious deployment plan.
